definition: Resplendent means dazzlingly splendid; gloriously bright.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word resplendent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know resplendent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The peacock fanned its tail and stood resplendent, a hundred green-gold eyes catching the sun.
Bright is plain light, far below resplendent — a hallway bulb manages bright, with no majesty anywhere in it.
Gleaming goes further than bright — surfaces polished until they flash — but it stops short of resplendent, which adds majesty to the shine: a whole presence lit up in glory.

Dazzling is light-first — anything bright enough can dazzle, from a welder's arc to headlights on high beam, and the word says nothing about grandeur. Resplendent asks for more: the eye must be overwhelmed and honored at once, with majesty riding on the light.

Magnificent means grand — by size, cost, or sheer ambition — and it needs no shine at all. Resplendent is narrower: reserved for visual glory, where light and majesty arrive together, so a thing must actually blaze before resplendent fits it.

The tall ship came up the channel for the festival resplendent: full sail set, forty signal flags snapping from her rigging, brass rails flashing, her bow carvings freshly leafed in gold.
Traffic stopped on the bluff road.
Children who had never cared about boats pointed and yelled.
She was, for one morning, the only thing worth looking at on that water.
Resplendent is the exact word for the ship that morning, because it means dazzlingly splendid, gloriously bright — light and majesty arriving together.
Dazzling alone could describe a welder's arc; resplendent insists the eye is overwhelmed and honored at once.
Resplendent is reserved for visual glory — light plus majesty.

Dazzling can describe any bright thing and magnificent any grand one; resplendent insists the eye is overwhelmed and honored at once, which is why it gravitates to ceremonies, plumage, treasure, and skies.
No unit-mate competes for its lane; just remember the re- is an intensifier, not 'again' — the word promises shining through and through, never shining twice.

For sixty years the Alhambra Theater sat dark, its chandelier crated in the basement and its gilded balconies painted over in gray.
The restoration crew worked from photographs taken on opening night, 1912, peeling the gray away to find gold leaf underneath.
On the night of the reopening, the chandelier rose to the dome on its original winch and its four hundred crystals caught the stage lights all at once.
A critic wrote that the old house was not merely bright again but resplendent: the light itself seemed ceremonial, as though the room had put on robes.
Ticket holders reportedly stopped in the doorway, unwilling to walk in and interrupt it.
